scope: Read-only independent review of dispatch.py, test_dependency.py, FINDINGS.md, evidence.json, tests.log, and pinned queue/executor validators. Ran bounded synthetic DAG and validator adversarial checks in temporary directories; did not edit author code or results.

verdict.supported_scope: No material dependency readiness or result-authentication defect found under the stated cooperating-client/trusted-mutable-SQLite and non-daemonizing executor contract.
verdict.production_status: Not production-ready; the documented mutable-storage, filesystem race, process-session, crash/power-loss, and operational gaps are real adoption blockers outside this research scope.
verdict.scientific_authority: None; native outputs are metadata-verified and qualification remains unassessed.

source_integrity.status: saved local pins match current reviewed files
source_integrity.saved_tests: Nine author tests pass in tests.log; evidence source manifests include dispatch, V2 admission, original queue/executor/ledger/receipt sources.

basis: Consumer binding resolves each dependency to an owner row in the same immutable plan, then calls verified_release; an existing release.json or successful-looking output alone is insufficient.

verified_release requires the SQLite release row, verifies canonical body/digest and exact result/release file pins, reconstructs the frozen producer binding/reservation, re-observes the original executor and recomputes the result, then checks the release document chain.

A producer must have outcome accepted_execution. Nonzero, timeout, invalid-native-output and other failed producer results do not authorize consumers. Unknown exit yields NotReady and retains capacity.

A consumer binding pins producer result, release, terminal and selected output; it inserts all four into the effective executor input pins and substitutes only declared SHA argv sentinels. Conflicting pins fail closed.
Reservation remains active until the release record commits. Release/result files published before SQLite commit do not count as readiness.
A consumer-first plan order skips the not-ready consumer and schedules its producer; after producer release, the next selection can bind the consumer.
If a file is tampered after binding or after executor preparation but before launch, current chain verification/input-pin checks retain the reservation without launch.
Selected terminal/recovery evidence pins are reverified; process/session observations, cooperative job lock, known return code and terminal cleanup verification gate release.
Each declared output path is checked for containment, re-pinned, required to match a native receipt from the terminal, and checked against its minimum byte threshold.
The generic evidence and native metadata do not certify scientific meaning or arbitrary nested input references; owner command validation and science remain external.

authentication_review.uncommitted_release_test: Passed author test: caller death after release.json publication leaves no release row and no consumer attempt; tampering retains capacity; restoring exact bytes allows recovery.
authentication_review.potential_race: Noncooperating filesystem writers can alter pinned files after checks and before/during consumer reads. Rechecking in dispatcher and original executor preparation/launch/child narrows but does not eliminate TOCTOU. The artifact correctly limits trust to cooperating local writers.

source_validation: Plan validator rejects unknown/self edges, unknown roles, duplicate producer-role edges, duplicate argv argument-slot use, unbound SHA sentinels, and cycles.
An edge includes job ID, native receipt role, exact fixed path argv slot(s), and SHA sentinel slot(s); output roles are unique within each job and outputs are disjoint through V2 admission.
Transitive three-job chain is covered by author test.

independent_synthetic_diamond.graph: producer p1 -> left and right; both left/right -> join; consumer/join listed before dependencies in plan.
independent_synthetic_diamond.observed: All four jobs released; join authenticated both producer release chains and wrote expected joined fixture payload; reserved count returned to zero.
independent_synthetic_diamond.isolation: Fresh TemporaryDirectory and invented child commands only; no owner files or persisted results touched.

independent_plan_validation.cycle: Two-node cycle rejected with dependency-cycle validation.
independent_plan_validation.branch_fanout: A producer with two consumers validates.

gaps: Author tests cover a simple transitive chain but not branching or multiple-parent joins; independent synthetic diamond closes this basic functional coverage gap, not exhaustive combinatorics.

Shared ancestors are recursively reauthenticated per dependency path with no scale bound or performance test; exponential/repeated verification is a scalability gap, not a small-fixture correctness failure.
Many-role, duplicate-path alias, very deep DAG and high fanout cases are not comprehensively tested.

crash_and_cleanup_review.assessment: Crash recovery is coherent for injected caller death at these points: no relaunch after launch-intent; precommit publications are compared exactly and recovered; SQLite release insertion rolls back on caller death before commit; committed release is recognized on retry.
not_proven: Actual power loss, filesystem/SQLite fsync behavior under hardware failure, syscall-level short-write or commit ambiguity, concurrent noncooperating writer races, and arbitrary kernel/process reparenting are not established by caller os._exit fixtures.

Process cleanup inherits the original Linux /proc, pidfd, flock and owned-session model. Escaping into a new session/daemonization is outside the stated cleanup scope and could outlive the observed owner process; production commands need a non-daemonization/containment contract or stronger isolation.
Cleanup proof is an executor-generated mutable local receipt, not an external attestation.

review: SQLite release/reservation triggers protect against ordinary API mutation, but a filesystem owner can drop triggers, coherently rewrite or roll back SQLite rows and documents, or replace the local config/source state.
Current selected chain is synchronously checked; unreferenced released history is not fully audited on each tick. No protected head/append-only log/independent storage anchor is supplied.
The specific commit gate is real: readiness requires a committed release row. Global capacity and old released-history truth remain under the trusted mutable-index contract.
storage_and_audit_trust.classification: Documented adoption gap, not a false-ready bug under its explicitly trusted database premise.

other_boundaries: Fresh initialization is not an atomic bootstrap or repair protocol; interrupted roots remain visible and require operator investigation.
Capacity one and one synchronous dispatcher lock are fixed; pending candidate selection and recursive chain checking have no measured scale guarantee.

No cancellation/prelaunch deferral, automatic orphan recovery, cross-plan outputs, external result authority, protected historical audit, unattended controller, or production migration is implemented.

Failed predecessor is released as a recorded failure and dependent remains pending/not-ready; it is not silently run or falsely reported complete. No policy for scientifically appropriate handling of failed/unknown branches is supplied.

adoption_blockers: Replace or formally accept mutable SQLite/config and no rollback protection; define external audit/recovery authority.
Establish filesystem trust/atomicity and command containment, including no daemonized descendants or a stronger sandbox/cgroup boundary.
Test concurrent clients, machine/power-loss boundaries and recovery on supported deployment storage; current tests use local Linux and synthetic jobs.
Add operational policy for stale/unknown reservations, dependency failure, cancellation and operator intervention before unattended use.
coverage_gaps_not_demonstrated_failures: Full combinatorial DAG and scale testing; the small diamond passed.
Durable audit of all released history and robust storage-level trust anchoring.
Scientific authorization/qualification, fit/prediction execution, and model promotion.

reproduction.why: Saved tests.log reviewed; bounded independent synthetic diamond and validator checks exercised required DAG paths without rerunning or editing author output.
independent_commands: Temporary real-executor synthetic diamond DAG (3.5 seconds).
Direct queue plan-validator checks for two-node cycle rejection, duplicate edge rejection and branch fanout acceptance.
